scope: AST inventory of all seven pinned JavaScript files; comments are excluded. Index script and dynamically compiled handler execution still require source propagation checks.

semantics.clock: Unbounded exact elapsed clock; Date.now floors to integer milliseconds.
semantics.nativePrefix: Absolute value at most 8640000000000000 milliseconds. Preserve existing binary64 result while the exact arithmetic result remains in this range.
semantics.extendedArithmetic: Timestamp plus/minus a finite binary64 duration uses its exact dyadic value outside the native prefix. Reentry rounds once to binary64.
semantics.difference: Timestamp minus timestamp projects the exact difference to ordinary binary64; two native-prefix operands use the existing Number.sub directly.
semantics.numericProjection: Timestamp multiply/divide/remainder/bitwise and explicit Number conversion leave the clock domain by binary64 projection. This does not make ordinary economic arithmetic exact.
semantics.calendar: Exact UTC Gregorian calendar. Outside the native Date prefix, civil years and Easter intermediate arithmetic use a separate exact rational carrier; date construction truncates components as native source does.
semantics.save: Eight listed current-save timestamp fields and the separate MAIL timestamp use source-checked typed readers. Main lumpT is intentionally floored. The user selected total processing of timestamp-derived UTF-16 text beyond native string/index limits; the retained mixkey activation and native save-codec operations now carry that text provenance. Complete source propagation and tagged-loop termination proofs remain open. Ordinary cookie/counter parsers are unchanged.
semantics.quota: The native 104857600-byte storage quota still applies. The selected timestamp-text extension does not remove storage quota or prove late reload success.

unresolvedChoices: The unbounded-clock assumption alone does not select out-of-range arithmetic rules; exact dyadic duration arithmetic is the selected extension, not native JavaScript behavior.
The implemented calendar scalar covers source Easter and expiry arithmetic. A general whole-source propagation invariant and any additional calendar crossings still require proof.
